rows.label: Yearly earnings gain per standard deviation of test scores
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's assumption, in its 2019 education work, for how much more a person earns each year for each standard deviation their test scores rose at school. Its range runs from its pessimistic (10th percentile) to its optimistic (90th) case. FP's note: it depends on education level, test type, persistence, country and labour market. The same 10% is used in its evidence-based policy sheet for J-PAL's Zambia reform.

rows.label: Share of the earnings gain that is additional
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's judgment of how much of the earnings gain is new income rather than income taken from others (for example, better-schooled workers winning jobs others would have had). Range from its pessimistic to its optimistic case.

rows.label: Years from schooling to the start of the earnings gain
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge assumes primary-school pupils start earning about eight years after the program. The same in all its cases and in its policy sheet's Zambia tab.

rows.label: Years the earnings gain lasts
rows.explainer: How long Founders Pledge assumes the earnings gain lasts: 5 years in its balanced case, 2 to 20 across its pessimistic and optimistic cases. Short, because test-score gains from school programs often fade.
